title: Senior's toolkit: finding coupling in history, removing it in code
summary: Use git history to see what changes together, and records and read-only types to stop it spreading.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: finding coupling in history, removing it in code
steps.body: Hidden coupling shows up in git before it shows up in a diagram: files that always change together, a function rewritten every sprint. Seniors read that history first, then use immutable types so a change in one place cannot leak into another.

toolkit.what: The full history of one function: every commit that changed it, with only that function's diff. Great for "why is this here?".
flags: follow the function whose header matches Name

toolkit.what: Every commit that touched Tax.cs, listing **all** the files in each commit. Files that keep appearing are coupled to it, whatever the code says.
flags: show the whole commit, not only the path you filtered on
file names instead of the diff

toolkit.cmd: git log --format=format: --name-only --since=6.months | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
toolkit.what: Hotspots: the files changed most often recently. A file that is both big and a hotspot is where coupling costs the most.
flags: print no commit header, only the file names
toolkit.example: git log --format=format: --name-only --since=6.months -- src/ | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20

toolkit.what: Who last changed each line, and in which commit. Without the flags, a reformat or a moved block hides the real author.
flags: find lines moved or copied from other files

toolkit.what: The history of a file across renames. Without `--follow` the log stops at the commit that moved it.
flags: keep going through renames (one file only)

toolkit.what: An immutable type with value equality. Nobody can change an address you passed them, so callers cannot couple through shared state. `with` makes a changed copy.
flags: properties are `init`-only; two records with equal values are `==`
the same for a small value type, with no heap allocation
toolkit.example:
public readonly record struct Money(decimal Amount, string Currency);
var moved = address with { City = "Leeds" };

toolkit.what: Expose a read-only view of a collection, so callers can look but only the owner can change it. Use `ImmutableArray<T>` when the data must never change at all.
flags: a view: callers cannot Add or Remove
truly immutable; changes return a new array
wrap a List<T> so a cast back to List fails
toolkit.example:
private readonly List<OrderLine> _lines = [];
public IReadOnlyList<OrderLine> Lines => _lines.AsReadOnly();

steps.prompt: A change to tax rounding in `Tax.cs` broke shipping estimates, which live in another project. Which command best shows what else usually changes together with `Tax.cs`?
steps.explain: Without `--full-diff`, filtering on a path also hides every other file in the commit. With it you see that `Estimate.cs` changed in 7 of the last 9 tax commits: hidden coupling, probably a shared constant or a shared mutable object.

steps.prompt: Match each option to what it adds.
pairs: keeps a file's history across renames
finds lines moved from other files
lists every file of each matching commit

steps.prompt: You want the history of the method `ApplyDiscount`, then the real author of each line even though the file was reformatted last month.
steps.explain: `-L :name:file` follows a function. `-w` makes blame skip whitespace changes, so the reformat commit does not take credit for every line.

code: var a = new Address("1 High St", "York");
steps.explain: `with` copies; the original is untouched, so whoever else holds `a` is not affected. Records compare by value, so a separately built address with the same values is equal.

items: How has `CalculateTax` changed over the last year?
When did someone add the `if (country == "IE")` branch to this method?
Who wrote line 48, ignoring last month's reformat?
This block was moved here from `Helpers.cs`: who really wrote it?
The file was renamed from `TaxCalc.cs`: show all of its history
The log for `Tax.cs` starts in March, but the code is older

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Before a refactor, spend two minutes in the history: hotspots tell you where coupling hurts, and `--full-diff` tells you what moves together. When two parts share data, pass an immutable record or a read-only view instead of a mutable object, so neither can change the other behind its back.
